games.name: Historia Yetu
games.line: Maswali za history ya 254 — primary na high school, from Turkana Boy to Katiba 2010. Uko sure unajua?

games.name: Unasema Sheng?
games.line: Keja, mbogi, nduthi, luku. Tuone kama uko fiti na lugha ya mtaa.

games.name: Methali
games.line: Haraka haraka… Mgeni njoo… Finish the Swahili proverb before the clock does.

games.name: Kaunti Gani?
games.line: All 47 counties — Mandera to Kwale, Kakuma to Kit Mikayi. Unajua ziko wapi?

games.name: Kichwa Juu
games.line: Phone on your forehead, the mbogi acts it out. Matatu tout, smokie pasua, Kipchoge — guess fast.

games.name: Ungependa?
games.line: Githeri for a month or no chapo ever? Would-you-rather for the whole table.

games.name: Chora!
games.line: Draw it on the phone, your team guesses before time's up. Matatu, twiga, ugali…

games.name: Bei Gani?
games.line: A real price off the Bamboo Cask menu. Slide to your number; the closer you land, the more it scores.

games.name: Kumbukumbu
games.line: Flip two, find the pair. Real dishes and bottles from the menu, and a sharp memory.

games.name: Guess the Bottle
games.line: A bottle from the Cask Room steps out of the dark. Name it before the light comes up.

games.name: Perfect Pour
games.line: Hold to pour, let go on the line. A barman's hand, or a beginner's?

games.name: Bar Trivia
games.line: Ten questions on Kenyan drinks, the bar and the bottle.

games.name: Spin the Bottle
games.line: Names round the table, a bottle in the middle, and a dare for whoever it picks.

history: The fossil skeleton nicknamed 'Turkana Boy' was found at…
Kamoya Kimeu found him in 1984 — one of the most complete Homo erectus skeletons ever found.
Proconsul, an early ape fossil, was found by Mary Leakey on…
Rusinga Island in Lake Victoria, 1948 — about 18 million years old.
Olorgesailie, in Kajiado, is famous for…
Acheulian hand-axes, left by Homo erectus hundreds of thousands of years ago.
Which early human is called 'handy man' for making the first stone tools?
Homo habilis — 'handy man' — made the earliest Oldowan tools.
Which early human is believed to be the first to use fire?
Homo erectus — 'upright man' — used fire and made hand-axes.
Koobi Fora, a great fossil site, lies…
On the slopes of Mount Kenya
East of Lake Turkana, in Marsabit County — Richard Leakey's team worked there from 1968.
Hyrax Hill, a prehistoric site, is near…
Nakuru — it shows a Neolithic settlement and burial ground.
The Stone Age is divided into…
Early, Middle and Late Stone Age — by the tools people made.
The Nile valley and the 'Fertile Crescent' of Mesopotamia, about 10,000 years ago.
Ancient Egypt. Mesopotamia wrote in cuneiform.
Meroe, in ancient Sudan, was famous for…
Iron working — it was called the 'Birmingham of Africa'.
Kenya's peoples are grouped by language into…
Bantu, Nilotes and Cushites — the three language families.
The Bantu are believed to have come from…
West and Central Africa — the Cameroon–Congo region
West and Central Africa — they spread east and south over many centuries.
The Luo are River-Lake Nilotes who came from…
Bahr el Ghazal in South Sudan, following the Nile south.
The first Luo settlement in Kenya is traditionally Ramogi Hill, in…
Got Ramogi in Siaya — named after the leader Ramogi Ajwang'.
The Maasai, Samburu, Turkana and Iteso are…
The Kalenjin are Highland Nilotes. Their traditional cradle is…
Mount Elgon (Tulwop Kony) — they spread out from there.
The Somali, Borana, Rendille and Gabbra are…
Eastern Cushites, from the Ethiopian highlands and the Horn.
The Mijikenda trace their origin to…
Shungwaya, in southern Somalia — they moved south under pressure from the Oromo.
Nine homesteads — the nine Mijikenda communities, from the Giriama to the Digo.
The Agikuyu, Embu, Meru and Akamba are…
The Mount Kenya and Eastern Bantu.
The Abaluhya, Abagusii and Abakuria are…
The Ameru tradition says they came from a place called…
Mbwa — often placed on the coast.
One result of the migrations into Kenya was…
Peoples intermarried, traded and borrowed customs — like circumcision and age-sets.
The Nandi were led by a spiritual and political leader called the…
The Orkoiyot — Koitalel arap Samoei was the most famous.
The Maasai spiritual leader was called the…
The Oloibon, or Laibon — Mbatian and his son Lenana were famous Laibons.
The Wanga kingdom was ruled by a king with the title…
Nabongo — Nabongo Mumia is the best known.
The Ameru council of elders is called…
Njuri Ncheke — it still meets at Nchiru, in Meru.
Among the Luo, a chief was called the…
Ruoth — he ruled with a council of elders.
The Mijikenda lived in fortified forest villages called…
Kaya — the sacred kaya forests are now a World Heritage Site.
Among the Agikuyu, power was handed between generations in a ceremony called…
Itwika — the ruling generation handed over to the next.
The Kalenjin village council of elders was the…
Thimlich Ohinga, in Migori, is a set of…
Dry-stone enclosures, built without mortar about 500 years ago — a World Heritage Site since 2018.
Before colonial rule, the Akamba were best known as…
Long-distance traders — taking ivory to the coast.
An Akamba caravan leader — the missionary Krapf travelled with him.
In traditional Kenyan societies, history was passed on mainly by…
Oral tradition — stories, songs and sayings
By word of mouth: stories, songs, proverbs and riddles.
Age-sets in traditional society were groups of…
People initiated at the same time
People who went through initiation together — they stayed bound for life.
Traders crossed the Indian Ocean to the East African coast using…
The monsoon winds — north-east to Africa, south-west back to Arabia and India.
Bantu languages with many Arabic words
A Bantu language that borrowed widely from Arabic — and later Persian, Portuguese and English.
Gedi, an old Swahili town now in ruins, is near…
Watamu in Kilifi — abandoned around the 1600s.
The Chinese admiral Zheng He's fleet visited the Kenyan coast in the 1400s. Malindi sent China a…
A giraffe — the Chinese court thought it was a mythical qilin.
The traveller Ibn Battuta visited Mombasa in…
1331 — he admired its mosques and people.
The most valuable export from the interior to the coast in the 1800s was…
Ivory — along with, tragically, enslaved people.
Seyyid Said moved his capital from Muscat to…
Zanzibar, around 1840 — and made it a centre of cloves and trade.
The Zanzibar slave market was closed in…
1873, under a treaty Sultan Barghash signed with Britain.
Frere Town near Mombasa was founded for…
Freed slaves, by the Church Missionary Society in 1875.
Mombasa, for much of the 1700s and early 1800s, resisting the Busaidi of Zanzibar.
The first Portuguese explorer to reach the Kenyan coast, in 1498, was…
Vasco da Gama — the Sultan of Malindi welcomed him and gave him a pilot to India.
Vasco da Gama's pillar still stands in…
Malindi — the friendly town that helped him reach India.
Fort Jesus was built by the Portuguese in…
1593, to control Mombasa and the sea route to India.
The Omani Arabs captured Fort Jesus in 1698 after a siege of…
About 33 months, from 1696 to 1698 — the end of Portuguese rule on the coast.
One reason the Portuguese came to East Africa was to…
To control the rich Indian Ocean trade and the sea route to India.
One thing the Portuguese introduced to East Africa was…
Crops like maize, cassava and groundnuts
Crops from the Americas — maize, cassava, groundnuts, pineapples.
The first Christian missionary in Kenya, who arrived in 1844, was…
Johann Ludwig Krapf, of the Church Missionary Society.
The first mission station in Kenya was opened in 1846 at…
Rabai, near Mombasa — by Krapf and Rebmann.
The first European to see Mount Kilimanjaro, in 1848, was…
Johannes Rebmann. Krapf saw Mount Kenya the next year, 1849.
Krapf is remembered for writing the first…
A Swahili dictionary and grammar — and he translated parts of the Bible into Kiswahili.
Count Teleki named a lake after Prince Rudolf in 1888. Today it is called…
Thomson's Falls in Nyahururu is named after the explorer…
Joseph Thomson, who crossed Maasailand in 1883.
John Hanning Speke is remembered for identifying the source of the Nile as…
Schools, hospitals and literacy — alongside Christianity.
The Berlin Conference that divided Africa among European powers was held in…
1884–85, chaired by Germany's Otto von Bismarck.
The 1890 Heligoland Treaty between Britain and Germany…
Settled who controlled Kenya, Uganda and Tanganyika
Germany got Tanganyika, Britain got Kenya and Uganda — Germany got the island of Heligoland.
The Imperial British East Africa Company was led by…
Sir William Mackinnon. It was chartered in 1888.
Britain declared the East Africa Protectorate in…
1895, taking over from the bankrupt IBEA Company.
Kenya became a British colony in…
Mombasa, in 1896. It reached Kisumu — then Port Florence — in 1901.
Most of the workers who built the Uganda Railway came from…
India — about 32,000 indentured labourers. Many stayed and their families are Kenyans today.
1899 — a swamp the Maasai called Enkare Nyirobi, 'place of cool waters'.
Before Nairobi, the capital of the British East Africa Protectorate was…
Mombasa. The capital moved to Nairobi in the early 1900s.
A registration document Africans had to carry
A kind of tax on huts
An identity and labour document worn around the neck — hated, and later burnt in protest.
The hut tax was introduced mainly to…
Force Africans to work for settlers and pay for the colony
To raise money and force Africans into wage labour.
The fertile land reserved for European settlers was called…
The White Highlands — in the central highlands and Rift Valley.
The Sultan of Zanzibar — Britain leased it, and it joined Kenya at independence.
The British ruled Kenya mainly through…
Indirect rule, using chiefs and headmen
Direct rule by British officers in every village
Indirect rule — through appointed chiefs and headmen.
The settler leader who pushed wheat and dairy farming in the highlands was…
Lord Delamere — the settlers' leader for decades.
The Devonshire White Paper of 1923 declared that in Kenya…
'African interests must be paramount' — mostly to block Indian demands.
A.M. Jeevanjee, the Indian businessman, gave Nairobi…
Jeevanjee Gardens, in 1906. He was also the first Indian on the Legislative Council.
The Swynnerton Plan of 1954 allowed Africans to…
Grow cash crops like coffee and consolidate land
Grow cash crops like coffee and tea, and own consolidated, titled land.
During the First World War, thousands of Kenyans served as porters in the…
The Carrier Corps — Nairobi's Kariokor is named after it.
In the Second World War, Kenyan soldiers of the King's African Rifles fought in…
Burma and Ethiopia, among others — they came home asking why they had no rights.
Koitalel arap Samoei led the resistance of the…
The Nandi — they fought the British for about ten years until he was killed in 1905.
Mekatilili wa Menza led the resistance of the…
The Agiriama, in 1913–14 — she was detained in Gusiiland and walked home.
The Nandi resisted the British partly because…
Their Orkoiyot prophesied a snake would cross their land — the railway
They were allies of the Germans
A prophecy that an 'iron snake' would bring trouble — the railway.
Waiyaki wa Hinga resisted the IBEA Company at…
Dagoretti, around 1890. He died in 1892 on the way to the coast.
The Bukusu fought the British at the Battle of…
Among the Abagusii, resistance was inspired by the prophetess…
Moraa — and in 1908 Otenyo speared the British officer Geoffrey Northcote.
The Maasai leader who collaborated with the British was…
Laibon Lenana — Point Lenana on Mount Kenya is named after him.
Nabongo Mumia of the Wanga collaborated with the British. Which town is named after him?
Mumias — he helped the British extend rule across Western Kenya.
The Maasai lost much of their land through the Anglo-Maasai agreements of…
1904 and 1911 — moved first to Laikipia, then to a southern reserve.
Wangu wa Makeri is remembered as…
The only woman appointed a colonial chief among the Agikuyu
The only Kikuyu woman colonial chief, in Murang'a.
The Young Kikuyu Association, then the East African Association, in 1921.
When Harry Thuku was arrested in 1922, the protest at the Nairobi police station was led by…
Mary Muthoni Nyanjiru — she and others were shot dead.
The Kikuyu Central Association's newspaper, edited by Jomo Kenyatta, was called…
Jomo Kenyatta's book about Gikuyu life, published in 1938, is…
Facing Mount Kenya. (Not Yet Uhuru is Oginga Odinga's; Unbowed is Wangari Maathai's.)
The first African member of the Legislative Council, in 1944, was…
The Kenya African Union (KAU) began in 1944 as the…
The Kenya African Study Union. Kenyatta became its president in 1947.
The Ukamba Members Association of 1938 protested against…
Forced destocking — led by Samuel Muindi Mbingu.
John Owalo founded Kenya's first independent church, the…
Elijah Masinde led the Bukusu movement called…
Githunguri Teachers' College, run by Kenyans for Kenyans, was headed by…
Jomo Kenyatta, from 1947 — part of the independent schools movement.
The State of Emergency in Kenya was declared on…
20 October 1952, by Governor Sir Evelyn Baring — now Mashujaa Day.
Leaders tried and jailed by the colonial government
Mau Mau generals in the forest
Six chiefs who helped the British
Kenyatta, Bildad Kaggia, Kung'u Karumba, Fred Kubai, Paul Ngei and Achieng' Oneko.
Which of these was NOT one of the Kapenguria Six?
Tom Mboya — he was a trade unionist in Nairobi at the time.
Dedan Kimathi was captured in 1956 near…
Nyeri. He was executed in February 1957. His statue stands on Kimathi Street.
Mau Mau fighters were based mainly in…
The Aberdares and Mount Kenya forests
The Aberdare ranges and Mount Kenya forests.
The killing of eleven detainees at a detention camp
Eleven detainees were beaten to death at Hola camp — it shocked Britain and sped up change.
Field Marshal Muthoni wa Kirima was…
A Mau Mau fighter who kept her dreadlocks uncut for decades after the war.
The first African minister, appointed under the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954, was…
B.A. Ohanga, Minister for Community Development.
Africans first elected members to the Legislative Council in…
1957 — eight African members, including Tom Mboya, Oginga Odinga and Daniel arap Moi.
The constitutional talks that led to independence were held at…
KANU and KADU were both formed in…
KADU's policy of regional government was called…
Majimbo — it was in the independence constitution, then scrapped.
Jomo Kenyatta was released from detention in…
Tom Mboya's 'airlifts' sent hundreds of young Kenyans to study in…
The United States, from 1959 — Barack Obama Sr. was one of them.
Internal self-government on 1 June 1963, six months before full independence.
12 December 1964 — exactly a year after independence, with Kenyatta as president.
Mzee Jomo Kenyatta, from 1964 until he died in 1978.
Malcolm MacDonald — also the last colonial governor.
Who led Kenya after Moi, from 2002 to 2013?
Kenya's fifth president, sworn in in 2022, is…
William Ruto, sworn in on 13 September 2022.
Footsteps — following in Kenyatta's. Its motto: peace, love and unity.
Sessional Paper No. 10 of 1965 set out Kenya's policy of…
'African Socialism and its Application to Planning in Kenya', associated with Tom Mboya.
Oginga Odinga left KANU in 1966 to form the…
The KPU — it was banned in 1969.
Tom Mboya was assassinated in Nairobi in…
Kenya's first post-independence political assassination, in 1965, was of…
Pio Gama Pinto, a freedom fighter and journalist.
Jomo Kenyatta died in 1978 at State House…
Section 2A, added to the constitution in 1982, made Kenya…
A one-party state, by law. It was repealed in December 1991.
The attempted coup of 1 August 1982 was led by soldiers of the…
The Kenya Air Force — it failed within hours.
A rally for multi-party democracy, called by Kenneth Matiba and Charles Rubia.
Kenya's first multi-party general election since the 1960s was held in…
Won — the draft constitution was rejected
Orange (No) won. The movement became ODM — the Orange Democratic Movement.
The deal that ended the 2007–08 post-election crisis was mediated by…
Kofi Annan — the National Accord created a Grand Coalition with Raila Odinga as Prime Minister.
In 2017 Kenya's Supreme Court made African history by…
Annulling the presidential result on 1 September 2017 — a first in Africa.
The 8-4-4 system of education began in…
1985 — now being replaced by the Competency-Based Curriculum.
Free primary education was introduced in 2003 by the government of…
Kenya's current constitution was promulgated in…
27 August 2010 at Uhuru Park, after the referendum of 4 August.
How many counties does Kenya have?
47 counties, each with its own governor, since 2013.
The three arms of government are…
The Legislature makes laws, the Executive carries them out, the Judiciary interprets them.
The National Assembly and the Senate
The House of Lords and Commons
The County Assembly and the Senate
The National Assembly and the Senate, since 2013.
The Supreme Court, created by the 2010 constitution. The Chief Justice heads it.
To vote in Kenya you must be at least…
18, a citizen, and registered with the IEBC.
Kenya's general elections are held every…
Five years, on the second Tuesday of August.
How many constituencies does Kenya have?
290 — each elects a Member of the National Assembly.
A county is led by a…
A Governor, with a County Assembly of MCAs making county laws.
The 2010 constitution's Bill of Rights is in…
Chapter Four. Chapter Eleven is devolution.
To win the presidency, a candidate needs more than half the votes and at least 25% in…
At least half of the counties
Kenya's first Chief Justice under the 2010 constitution was…
Willy Mutunga, from 2011. Martha Koome became the first woman Chief Justice in 2021.
The office of Deputy President was created by…
The 2010 constitution — William Ruto was the first, in 2013.
The body that runs elections in Kenya is the…
The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission.
English and Kiswahili — and Kiswahili is the national language.
Kenya's first woman elected MP, in 1969, was…
Grace Onyango, of Kisumu Town — she had been Kisumu's first woman mayor.
Kenya's first three elected women governors, in 2017, included…
Anne Waiguru, Charity Ngilu and Joyce Laboso
Martha Karua, Sabina Chege and Millie Odhiambo
Gladys Wanga, Susan Kihika and Fatuma Achani
Grace Onyango, Phoebe Asiyo and Julia Ojiambo
Anne Waiguru (Kirinyaga), Charity Ngilu (Kitui) and Joyce Laboso (Bomet).
Let's all pull together — on the coat of arms.
On the Kenyan flag, the red stands for…
The blood shed in the struggle. Black is the people, green the land, white peace.
On the flag, black stands for…
The shield and spears on the flag stand for…
'Ee Mungu nguvu yetu' — O God of all creation.
The tune of the national anthem came from…
A traditional Pokomo lullaby, arranged by a commission in 1963.
The coat of arms has two lions holding…
A shield and spears, standing on Mount Kenya — with a cockerel holding an axe on the shield.
Mashujaa Day, 20 October, used to be called…
Kenyatta Day — renamed Heroes' Day by the 2010 constitution.
The 2010 constitution names Kenya's national symbols as the flag, the anthem, the coat of arms and the…
The Central Bank of Kenya and the Kenya shilling were established in…
The Organisation of African Unity was founded in Addis Ababa in…
May 1963. It became the African Union in 2002.
The original East African Community collapsed in…
Which UN body has its global headquarters in Nairobi?
UNEP, at Gigiri — and UN-Habitat too.
Kenyatta and Nkrumah both attended the Pan-African Congress of 1945 in…
The first sub-Saharan African country to win independence from colonial rule, in 1957, was…
Which African country defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa in 1896?
Ethiopia, under Emperor Menelik II — it was never colonised.
The Maji Maji rebellion (1905–07) was against German rule in…
Tanganyika — Kinjikitile told fighters that 'maji' (water) would turn bullets into water.
The Shona and Ndebele risings of 1896–97 in Zimbabwe are called the first…
The British colonial system of 'indirect rule' was most famously used by Lord Lugard in…
The French policy of making Africans 'French' in culture was called…
Assimilation — tried most fully in Senegal's Four Communes.
The First World War began after the assassination of…
Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria, in Sarajevo, 1914.
The Second World War began in 1939 when Germany invaded…
The United Nations was founded in…
1945, after the Second World War. Kenya joined on 16 December 1963.
The steam engine that powered the Industrial Revolution was improved by…
Apartheid in South Africa ended with the 1994 election of…
Nelson Mandela, after 27 years in prison.
The Kabaka of Buganda signed the 1900 agreement that made Buganda part of…
Wangari Maathai made history in 2004 as…
The first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize
The first woman to climb Mount Kenya
The first African woman Nobel laureate — for the Green Belt Movement, founded in 1977.
A railway depot on the Uganda Railway
The Lunatic Express — critics said it was madness to build.
Two maneless lions that attacked railway workers in 1898.
Kenya's first Olympic gold medal, in 1968, was won by…
Naftali Temu, 10,000m, Mexico City. Kip Keino won the 1,500m days later.
Eliud Kipchoge ran the first marathon under 2 hours in…
Lamu Old Town is famous as…
The oldest lived-in Swahili town in East Africa
A UNESCO World Heritage Site, lived in for over 700 years.
Kenya's highest mountain, Mount Kenya, reaches…
5,199 m at Batian. 5,895 m is Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania.
The Tana — it runs from the Aberdares and Mount Kenya to the Indian Ocean.
Which of these countries does NOT border Kenya?
Rwanda. Kenya's neighbours are Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Somalia.
The Equator passes through Kenya. Which town is on it?
Nanyuki — the Equator crosses Kenya from Lake Victoria to the Somali border, past Maseno, Nanyuki and Meru.
The University of Nairobi became Kenya's first full university in…
1970. It began as the Royal Technical College in 1956.
Kenya Defence Forces entered Somalia in 2011 in an operation called…
Kilindini Harbour, Mombasa — the gateway for much of East Africa.
sheng: Msee = a person. 'Wasee' = people. 'Msee wangu' = my guy.
A parent or an elder — often your dad
Mzae = old man, parent. 'Wazae' = the parents.
Manzi = a girl. So is 'dem' and 'mresh'.
Beshte = best friend, from 'best'. 'Mabeshte' = the besties.
Mdosi = the boss, the one with the money.
Sonko = a rich person, a big spender.
Kanjo = the county council askaris — the hawkers' worst enemy.
Fala = a fool. Don't call your mdosi one.
Makanga = the conductor who collects fare and hangs off the door.
Hamsa = fifty shillings, from the Arabic for five.
Kusota = to be broke. Mwisho wa mwezi, wote tumesota.
Kuomoka = to make it big. Sote tutaomoka.
Kutoboa = to break through, to make it. 'Mwaka huu tunatoboa.'
Your side business, how you make money
Hustle = the grind, how you make your money.
Ocha = upcountry, shags, home for December.
Nduthi = motorbike, the boda boda you hop on.
A pimped-out matatu with graffiti and loud music
Nganya = the flashy matatu with art, lights and a sound system.
Kuboeka = to be bored. Ukiboeka, cheza Kichwa Juu.
Fiti = fine, sawa. 'Niko fiti' = I'm good.
Noma = intense, mad. 'Ngoma hii ni noma!' = this song is fire.
To have a great time, be excited
Kuhanya = to cheat. 'Amehanyiwa' = they've been cheated on.
Kuchomeka = to be caught out, in trouble.
Kucheki = to see, check. 'Tucheki baadaye' = see you later.
Kuhepa = to bounce, to leave. 'Nimehepa' = I'm out.
Luku = your look. Kupiga luku = to dress to impress.
'Luku' yako iko fiti. What are they praising?
Kukam = to come, from English. 'Kam hapa!'
Kuchapa kazi = to work, to grind.
Mchongoano = the art of the roast. 'Wewe ni mfupi mpaka…'
Niaje? = what's up? Reply: 'Poa', 'Fiti' or 'Si mbaya'.
Which school form are you in?
Form = the plan, what's happening. 'Form ni gani leo?'
Stori = news, gossip, what's going on.
Ngoma = a song. 'Hii ngoma ni noma!'
methali: Hurry hurry has no blessing — rushing spoils things.
Slowly, slowly is the way to go — steady wins.
The patient one eats the ripe fruit.
Be late, but arrive — better late than never.
Wait, wait hurts the stomach — too much waiting has its own cost.
Carefully is the way to go.
Little by little fills the measure — small savings add up.
Chip by chip finishes the log — keep at it and the job gets done.
Where there's a will, there's a way.
Whoever wants what's under the bed must bend down — no effort, no reward.
If you see things floating, someone built them — nothing comes without work.
Whoever earns in the sun eats in the shade — hard work pays later.
Whoever is choosy about the hoe is no farmer — a worker doesn't make excuses.
Whoever won't accept defeat is no competitor — be a good loser.
Getting lost is how you learn the way — mistakes teach.
Whoever won't listen to elders breaks a leg — ignore advice at your own risk.
If you don't fill a crack, you'll build a wall — fix small problems early.
Spilt water can't be gathered back — think before you act.
A stick far away won't kill the snake — help you can't reach is no help.
Bend the fish while it's fresh — teach children while they're young.
Whoever isn't taught by their mother will be taught by the world.
Whoever won't let the child cry ends up crying — discipline now saves tears later.
Better to stub your toe than your tongue — careless words hurt more.
Wisdom is like hair — everyone has their own.
Someone with eyes doesn't need to be told to look.
Don't leave your old mat for a passing prayer mat — don't drop the sure thing for a fling.
The sign of rain is clouds — trouble shows itself before it comes.
Every vessel rides its own wave — everyone faces their own challenges.
You don't know the bedbugs of a bed you haven't slept in — don't judge from outside.
If you see your neighbour being shaved, wet your own head — learn from what happens to others.
Whoever rides two horses splits — you can't do two things at once.
To live long is to see much.
Knowledge is an ocean — you never finish learning.
Regret is a grandchild — it always comes last.
Wealth without records vanishes without trace — keep your books.
The ear doesn't grow above the head — respect your elders.
One finger can't crush a louse — we need each other.
Unity is strength, division is weakness.
One hand can't raise a child — it takes a village.
Where many gather, God is there.
Log against log is how the fire burns — togetherness keeps things alive.
Blood is thicker than water — family first.
A friend in need is a friend indeed.
Someone else's load feels as light as a bag of kapok — until you carry it.
Come, guest, so the host may prosper — visitors bring blessings.
When elephants fight, the grass suffers — the small people pay for the quarrels of the big.
Two bulls can't share one pen — two strong leaders clash.
A thief's days are forty — sooner or later, they're caught.
A liar's road is short — lies get found out.
A promise is a debt — keep your word.
Anger is loss — losing your temper costs you.
Greed in front, death behind — greed leads to ruin.
Dip by dip finishes the gourd of honey — small takings empty the store.
A donkey's thanks is a kick — some repay kindness with harm.
A good thing sells itself, a bad one has to be hawked.
A good name shines in the dark.
Kindness never rots — good deeds are remembered.
Sweet words draw the snake out of its hole — kindness persuades.
Whoever digs a well falls in it — plot harm and it lands on you.
Whoever climbs a ladder comes down — stay humble on the way up.
The tongue bites harder than teeth — words wound.
There's no secret between two people.
What roars loudest doesn't last — hype fades.
The lion that moves quietly is the one that eats — doers don't boast.
A snake's child is a snake — like parent, like child.
The village rooster doesn't crow in town — you're a big shot only at home.
Everything that has a beginning has an end.
When the cat's away, the mice rule.
What eats you is in your own clothes — trouble often comes from those close to you.
